title: Binary search warm-up
description: A tiny example course: one lesson and two problems you can run.

items.title: What binary search really needs
First number at least target
statement: nums is sorted in increasing order. Return the index of the first number that is greater than or equal to target.
If every number is smaller than target, return nums.length.

examples.explanation: 5 is the first number that is at least 4.

hints: The question 'is nums[mid] >= target?' flips from no to yes exactly once.
If it is yes, the answer is at mid or to its left. Otherwise it is to the right of mid.

idea: Binary search on the half-open range [0, n]: when nums[mid] >= target keep the left half including mid, otherwise move past mid.

items.title: Integer square root
statement: Return the largest integer r such that r * r <= x. Do not use a built-in square root.
hints: Search for the answer between 0 and x.
Compare mid * mid with x using 64-bit arithmetic to avoid overflow.
